description: Width tiers for Languages — Y7-10 Second Language Entry pathway, Year 7-8 band. All standards are capability descriptors (EC = communicating/interacting/mediating/creating; EU = understanding). EC strand standards use task_contexts as the primary width axis. EU strand standards use phenomena_contexts (for Language and Culture) or depth_fallback/phenomena_contexts (for Systems of Language).
subject: Languages

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context or phenomenon that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term. For EC strand standards: minimum is the narrowest communicative context in which the described interaction, mediation or creation is genuine — not modelled repetition of a single phrase. For EU strand standards: minimum is engagement with the described language feature in at least one familiar context with evidence of understanding.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope as ACARA intended — grounded in the most common elaboration cases. For EC strand: a range of task types and communicative contexts that cover the descriptor's communicative intent. For EU strand: the range of language features and contexts described in the elaborations.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new communicative contexts, cultural communities, comparison languages or task types. Width adds breadth of context — not difficulty of the same task. For EU strand: additional phenomena, languages for comparison, or cultural contexts that deepen the language understanding without exceeding the year band.
width_notes.elaborations: Spanish (Y7-10 Second Language Entry sequence) elaborations were used as the primary source. All target-language-specific examples have been genericised. Elaborations are preserved verbatim in each standard entry as source record.

AC9LS8EC01.minimum_width: Use modelled language to introduce themselves and exchange basic personal information (name, family, likes/dislikes) with a peer in at least one familiar context.
AC9LS8EC01.typical_width: Interact with others to exchange personal information across a range of familiar contexts — greetings, self-introduction, family, routines, leisure, significant events — using modelled language with appropriate formal/informal register choices. Conduct and respond to simple interviews about personal worlds.
wider: Interact with simulated or real target language community members about daily life — compare routines and personal worlds across cultural contexts
Extend exchanges to include past or upcoming events, connecting to emerging tense knowledge
Use a secure digital platform to exchange personal information in writing — compare conventions for digital personal exchange in the target language and English
elaborations: exchanging greetings with others using appropriate formal or informal language
introducing and describing themselves, others and possessions
expressing likes, dislikes and preferences using simple modelled structures
interviewing others about their families, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure time activities
responding to questions about feelings
conversing with others about routines, events and leisure activities using language associated with time and place
discussing significant or special events in their lives with peers or target language community members

AC9LS8EC02.minimum_width: Follow basic classroom commands and use at least two modelled phrases to ask for help or express an opinion in a classroom task context.
AC9LS8EC02.typical_width: Interact in the target language across classroom routine tasks — following and giving instructions, asking for help/permission/information, expressing opinions and reactions, participating in collaborative games and activities. Use spontaneous interjections and expressions to maintain simple interactions.
wider: Lead a classroom routine segment (roll call, task distribution, instructions) using only the target language
Design and facilitate a classroom game that requires target language use throughout — not only as a trigger for activity
Collect and compare asking and opinion expressions across formal and informal registers — identify contextual conventions
elaborations: responding appropriately to commands or requests
following and giving instructions
asking for help, information or permission
expressing opinions and thoughts using set phrases
assisting the teacher with classroom routines and duties
developing the use of spontaneous interjections, expressions and gestures to maintain simple interactions
playing games and completing activities with peers incorporating language to share, praise, encourage and take turns
making a simplified board game to reinforce learning vocabulary and grammatical points while playing with others
playing a true and false game relating to routines, interests and personal details

AC9LS8EC03.minimum_width: Participate in one structured exchange with a peer to organise or complete a simple joint activity using modelled target language.
AC9LS8EC03.typical_width: Engage in modelled non-verbal, spoken and written exchanges to organise and complete joint activities — collaborative resources, imagined scenarios, simulated transactions, digital messaging about plans. Coordinate across multiple communication modes (spoken, written, non-verbal).
wider: Use a secure digital platform to plan and carry out a real or simulated activity with a peer entirely in the target language
Navigate an authentic digital resource (map, timetable, service website) from a target language community to locate information for a real purpose
Produce a bilingual resource (poster, flyer, digital notice) that combines visual and written elements to communicate to a mixed-language audience
elaborations: working with peers to produce bilingual signs/flyers and posters to promote sustainability and waste reduction
working together to produce class reference materials such as wall charts or visuals to display key vocabulary and structures
participating in imagined scenarios such as asking for and giving directions, information and assistance
participating in real or simulated transactions such as purchasing food or tickets
emailing, messaging or using secure online applications to chat about plans and daily life experiences using present tense and immediate future

AC9LS8EC04.minimum_width: Locate at least three specific pieces of information from one familiar target language text type (e.g. menu, timetable, short notice) using basic comprehension strategies.
AC9LS8EC04.typical_width: Locate, classify and summarise information from a range of familiar spoken, written and multimodal target language texts — menus, notices, timetables, announcements, short recordings, film/story segments, digital maps. Respond to texts in ways that show awareness of cultural context, purpose and audience.
wider: Compare how the same type of information (e.g. transport, event details) is structured and presented in target language community texts vs Australian English equivalents
Locate and respond to texts by First Nations Australian authors presented in or alongside the target language — reflect on what is conveyed or lost in the cross-cultural encounter
Navigate an authentic digital resource from a target language community to locate information for a real or simulated purpose
elaborations: identifying details and key points of information from authentic resources or teacher-created texts
locating, classifying and summarising information collected from sources such as menus, notices, timetables, packaging or brochures
conducting simple surveys or interviews with others about familiar topics, then interpreting results
listening to, reading or viewing First Nations Australian authors' stories in English and responding to them in spoken or written target language
identifying key points of information in short spoken or recorded texts such as phone messages, announcements or television segments
identifying and describing characters and events in a movie, story or comic by responding to simple questions
navigating secure online applications such as digital maps or timetables to find out about transport and services in a target language community
locating specific information about a person, place or event, describing characters, events and locations

AC9LS8EC05.minimum_width: Use a dictionary to assist with the interpretation of a familiar target language text; identify at least one cognate and one false friend between the target language and English.
AC9LS8EC05.typical_width: Develop and begin to apply a set of interpretation strategies — dictionary use, cognate recognition, false friend awareness, contextual inferencing, understanding literal vs non-literal translation. Apply across short familiar texts (public signs, community notices, short conversations). Recognise that abbreviations and digital language conventions vary between languages.
wider: Evaluate an automated digital translation of a short target language text — identify specific errors and explain what the tool missed
Observe target language interactions in different contexts and identify how non-verbal and contextual cues support meaning where linguistic knowledge is incomplete
Investigate cognate patterns systematically — identify suffix or prefix patterns that reliably predict meaning in the target language and create a class reference resource
elaborations: translating short texts such as public signs or community notices from the target language to English, and vice versa, identifying parts that are difficult to translate
using print and online dictionaries to assist in the translation of simple texts
recognising cognates and the possibility of encountering false friends when translating between the target language and English
identifying cognate patterns that can be used to predict meaning or obtain gist
developing techniques to infer meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary and structures in a text
understanding the distinction between literal and non-literal translation
recognising that abbreviations are used in both the target language and English texts
observing live or recorded target language interactions in different contexts and recognising that communication extends beyond words
noticing variations in language use based on the age, gender and social relationships of speakers and the context and purpose of the communication

AC9LS8EC06.minimum_width: Create one spoken or written text in the target language (informative or imaginative) with a recognisable structure, a clear communicative intent, and vocabulary and grammar sufficient to convey meaning.
AC9LS8EC06.typical_width: Create spoken, written and multimodal texts across informative and imaginative text types — presentations, role-plays, informative posters/displays, simple narratives, performance texts. Apply appropriate vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions. Share and respond to questions about own texts.
wider: Create a bilingual text for a mixed-language audience — reflect on how structural and language choices change when the audience changes
Collaborate with a peer on a jointly-authored imaginative text — negotiate creative choices across the collaboration
Produce a text that promotes awareness of a relevant social or environmental issue — combine print, digital or visual elements for a specific audience
Plan and present a performance for non-target-language speakers, with bilingual and explanatory commentary
elaborations: preparing a presentation by following a format that includes a greeting, introduction and sequenced ideas
composing and performing a role-play based on a real or imagined scenario
producing informative texts that combine print, digital or visual elements for specific audiences
creating a print or digital poster to promote travel to a significant cultural location on a First Nations Country
creating resources such as posters or displays to create awareness of relevant issues
writing a story by composing captions for a sequence of pictures or images
creating characters, situations or events in a range of texts designed to entertain others
writing the first part of a short narrative and exchanging with a peer to write the next section
planning and presenting a performance for non-target-language speakers, with bilingual and explanatory commentary

AC9LS8EU01.minimum_width: Recognise and produce key target language vowel and consonant sounds that differ from English; demonstrate at least two distinct intonation patterns (statement vs question).
AC9LS8EU01.typical_width: Recognise and use features of the target language sound system — vowels, consonants, intonation, stress, pitch and rhythm — in familiar spoken and written contexts. Apply pronunciation rules; use phonological notes and marking conventions to support own production; transcribe short spoken texts using intonation cues.
wider: Research and compare pronunciation across two or more regional varieties of the target language — discuss what variation reveals about language change and cultural identity
Practise stress and rhythm through performance texts (poems, tongue twisters, songs) and reflect on how prosodic choices affect meaning or emphasis
Use recording tools to review own spoken target language production and identify specific phonological features to improve
elaborations: recognising that many letters of the target language and English have the same sounds, with some exceptions
understanding that in some target languages there is only one sound for each vowel
recognising and practising different vowel and consonant sounds through simple rhymes
spelling own name aloud in the target language
recognising variations in intonation required to form statements, questions and exclamations
listening to statements, exclamations and questions read aloud, using intonation cues and transcribing what is heard
using own phonetic notes to help pronunciation and intonation
applying pronunciation rules to common performance texts such as tongue twisters

AC9LS8EU02.minimum_width: Apply key orthographic conventions of the target language writing system; apply gender and number agreement in at least five familiar noun phrases; conjugate at least three regular verbs in the present tense.
AC9LS8EU02.typical_width: Develop knowledge of and use the target language grammatical and writing systems — orthographic conventions, grammatical gender and agreement, articles, adjectives, subject pronouns, verb conjugation (regular and common irregular forms) in affirmative/negative/interrogative, interrogative forms, prepositions, connectives. Apply in spoken, written and multimodal text production.
wider: Investigate how the target language's grammatical gender system works and compare with English — research how it is evolving in contemporary usage
Compare verb conjugation systems in the target language and English — identify what grammatical information the target language encodes in verb endings that English expresses differently
Explore the target language's pronoun system in depth — map formal/informal/plural distinctions and discuss how they encode social relationships
elaborations: recognising the number of consonants and vowels in the target language
noticing and applying different rules of capitalisation in the target language and English
identifying and applying graphic symbols specific to the target language on keyboards and in writing systems
understanding and applying grammatical gender rules
developing awareness of additional gender patterns in word endings
using appropriate definite and indefinite articles that agree in gender and number
understanding that adjectives and possessives agree in number and gender with nouns
developing knowledge of number and gender agreement with demonstratives
understanding the form and function of subject pronouns
understanding and using verb conjugations for the present tense of regular and common irregular verbs
recognising multiple versions of the verb 'to be' in some target languages
using verb conjugations in affirmative, negative and interrogative forms
seeking information using interrogatives
using prepositions of place and common contractions
linking ideas using connectives
recognising the functions of elements such as prefixes and suffixes

AC9LS8EU03.minimum_width: Identify and explain at least two grammatical or structural differences between the target language and English using familiar metalanguage.
AC9LS8EU03.typical_width: Compare key structures and features of the target language with English using metalanguage — verb systems, word order, syntax, register conventions, interrogative/negative constructions. Develop and use metalanguage in both languages to discuss grammatical structures. Compare text-level features of familiar text types across both languages.
wider: Investigate a grammatical feature present in the target language but absent in English (e.g. grammatical gender, formal/informal address distinctions) — explain what expressive or social function it serves
Research the influence of the target language on English or English on the target language — identify loan words and discuss what they reveal about cultural contact
Compare how digital communication conventions (abbreviations, emoticons, informal syntax) differ across the target language and English — identify what is shared and what is language-specific
elaborations: developing awareness that different verbs are used in the target language and English for certain expressions
identifying do/does as an interrogative/negative auxiliary in English and how it differs in the target language
understanding the difference in expressing decimal points and numbers in the target language and English
recognising that register shifts according to familiarity and social position
building metalanguage to understand and discuss grammatical structures and vocabulary in the target language and English
comparing key structures and features of familiar target language and English texts by identifying the intended purpose and audience
discussing target language and English word order and syntax, noticing similarities and differences
comparing the ways to express 'you' in the target language and equivalent forms in English
recognising the influence of target language culture(s) on English and other languages through loan words

AC9LS8EU04.minimum_width: Identify at least two ways in which the target language reflects cultural values, identity or social relationships; reflect on at least one connection between own language use and personal identity.
AC9LS8EU04.typical_width: Recognise how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — in target language communities and in own experience. Examine register as a reflection of social relationships; identify cultural references and values in target language texts and practices; consider how First Nations Australian languages encode connections to Country and community; compare culturally determined behaviours and communication styles.
wider: Investigate how multilingualism shapes identity in target language communities — research the experience of moving between languages and cultural identities
Examine how First Nations Australian languages encode connections to Country/Place/location and compare with how the target language encodes connection to community and place
Research how the target language continues to evolve through contact with other languages and cultures — identify specific examples of language change and discuss their causes
Create a personal text in the target language that expresses an aspect of own identity — discuss what was translatable and what required cultural explanation
elaborations: viewing interactions between target language speakers and recognising register as well as comparing culturally determined behaviours
listening to and reading traditional texts, identifying key messages, beliefs and values
identifying that a sense of identity and belonging is important across all cultures and discussing how it may be expressed differently
examining how First Nations Australian languages have strong connections to Country/Place location
exploring language features that reflect and embody cultural values and history, including regional differences
identifying elements of ways of communicating and behaving in the target language that may be unfamiliar to people from different cultural backgrounds
considering language use depending on context and relationship
understanding that languages and cultures change continuously due to contact with other languages and cultures
collecting examples of word borrowings from other languages
observing that many target language speakers may be multilingual and can move between languages to achieve different purposes
examining what is most important to them and their way of life
